text:
cheng: Heads-up, I pushed a new kernel-routing heuristic last night and the prefix cache dashboard shows a weird mid-day dip in hit-rate for /summarize and /extract routes. Screenshot: https://redwood.internal/snap/abc123 :thinking_face:
priya: saw that too, looks correlated with the kernel selection flip at 02:13 UTC (per deploy-bot).
deploy-bot: deploy completed: kernel-route-v2 -> services/serve-runtime @ 1755549200 :white_check_mark:
michael: quick numbers from telemetry: global prefix hit-rate fell from 62% -> 49% between 02:10-03:00, token-saved dropped ~27% for those routes.
sam: interestingly, the drop is concentrated on tenant slices with long contexts (>4k). short-context tenants unaffected.
cheng: my initial hypothesis: the new kernel picks a different batching path that changes KV cache keying for generated prefixes because of sequence-chunking alignment. Might be a key-normalization edge.
priya: can you paste the kernel-routing config that rolled?
cheng: sure, config snippet:
```
route_policy:
  - match: /summarize
    kernel: v2-optimize
    batch_hint: prefer_latency
  - match: /extract
    kernel: v2-optimize
    batch_hint: pack_by_sequence
```

cheng: note the pack_by_sequence change — it folds sequences differently which may shift prefix boundaries used by the cache key derivation.
michael: I pulled a small sample of KV keys before/after; keys now include a chunk-id suffix in ~18% of entries where previously they didn't. That explains lower dedupe.
sam: does warmup assume the old key shape? Warmup prefetcher samples prefixes and pumps them into the cache; if keying changed warmup misses.
priya: yes, warmup uses the key-normalizer lambda that strips chunk-id. If the runtime started including chunk-id in actual keys we get mismatch.
cheng: created quick mitigation: rollback kernel selection for those routes to v1-stable -> canary off. Rolling now.
deploy-bot: rollback initiated: kernel-route-v1-stable -> services/serve-runtime @ 1755551200
priya: while rollback lands, can we add an observability panel showing "key-shape drift" (ratio of keys with chunk suffix) per-tenant? Want to catch future regressions quicker.
michael: I'll add a derived metric: key_chunk_frac = count(keys_with_chunk_id)/count(keys_total) grouped by tenant, route, model.
tara: added a short sampling job to log first 100 key hashes for matched routes to S3 for inspection. Will run for next 30m.
sam: other action: update warmup normalizer to accept both shapes for a transitional period, then flip when we confirm stable. Patch in PR #4821.
cheng: also flagged a perf regression: the v2 kernel changed batching heuristic from "latency-first" to "throughput-pref" under moderate qps which increased average request latency by ~5ms for these routes; that probably pushed some requests into different batching cohorts and affected prefix alignment.
priya: good callout. Need two signals on dashboard: key_shape_drift and batch_cohort_shift (percent requests in each batching class).
michael: verbose profiling data attached: latency-by-batch-size, kernel-path, kv-lookup-distribution. Link: https://profiler/internal/run/2025-06-01/175555
cheng: TL;DR: root cause seems to be combined kernel batching heuristic + key-shape change -> warmup mismatch -> hit-rate drop. Rollback improves hit-rate in preliminary testing.
priya: next steps: (1) bake key-normalizer compatibility (PR #4821) (2) add key-shape and batch-cohort panels to daily dashboard (michael) (3) add smoke test that verifies warmup->cache key symmetry for new kernels (sam) (4) postmortem note if rollback completes (cheng).
sam: I'll own smoke test and PR, estimated 2 dev-days.
michael: I'll add panels and an alert: if token-saved delta > 15% vs baseline for any tenant, page oncall.
tara: sampling job running, will drop CSV to s3://redwood-debug/prefix-keys/175555/ by 1755555700.
cheng: thanks all — watching charts. :eyes: If rollback doesn't restore >95% of previous hit-rate by EOD, we'll escalate to runtime-team sync.
priya: also FYI, I'm scheduling a short postmortem sync at 11:30 to go over telemetry gaps and gating for kernel changes.
michael: preliminary patch to key-normalizer here: https://git.redwood/p/normalize-keys/+/4821 — handles both chunked and unchunked forms.
sam: noted, will include smoke harness test in that branch.
cheng: updating ticket INF-1342 with timeline and actions. Closing loop when charts green. :white_check_mark:
